description: OFSCP v0.1 WebSocket authenticate-handshake conformance vector (§7.1). Reconstruct the canonical string from the components, sign its UTF-8 bytes with Ed25519, base64-encode, and compare to expected.signature. The private key is a TEST key — never use it in production.
notes: The canonical string is four lines: <authority>, the literal domain separator ofscp-ws-authenticate, <challenge-nonce>, and <timestamp>.
Lines are joined with a single LF (0x0A); there is no trailing newline; all bytes are UTF-8.
<authority> uses §4.4.2 host canonicalization (lowercased, :port appended only when non-443).
<challenge-nonce> is the nonce from the server's auth.challenge event; binding it makes each authenticate usable on exactly one connection, once.
These values match tests/ws-auth-challenge.sample.json (nonce) and tests/ws-authenticate.sample.json (timestamp, signature).
Ed25519 signatures are deterministic, so this vector reproduces exactly.
